problem: Eden's conjecture that the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions on the global attractor is achieved on a stationary point or an unstable periodic orbit embedded into the attractor
missing_details: Definition of local Lyapunov dimension d_L(u) (finite-time Lyapunov exponents and Kaplan–Yorke formula)
Assumption of a continuously differentiable autonomous flow φ^t on U⊂ℝ^n
Definition of compact global attractor K and the fact that sup is over u∈K
Definition of unstable periodic orbit (closed trajectory with positive Lyapunov exponent)
refined_question: Let φ^t:U→U be the flow generated by a C¹ vector field f on an open set U⊂ℝ^n, and let K⊂U be its compact global attractor. For each u∈K define the local Lyapunov dimension d_L(u)=lim inf_{t→∞} d_KY({LE_i(t,u)}), where LE_i(t,u)=(1/t) ln σ_i(t,u) are the finite-time Lyapunov exponents given by the singular values σ_i of Dφ^t(u), and d_KY denotes the Kaplan–Yorke formula. Eden’s conjecture: is it true that sup_{u∈K} d_L(u) is attained either at an equilibrium point u_eq with f(u_eq)=0 or at a point on an unstable periodic orbit embedded in K?
justification: The original name states exactly that the supremum of local Lyapunov dimensions on the global attractor is achieved on a stationary point or unstable periodic orbit but omits the necessary definitions of the flow, attractor, and local dimension (cite Eden_statement). To make the question self-contained we specify a C¹ autonomous flow on ℝ^n with a compact global attractor K, define finite-time Lyapunov exponents and the local Lyapunov dimension via the Kaplan–Yorke formula, and clarify that the supremum is taken over all u∈K (cite Lyap_defs). The score 6/10 reflects that the name captures the core claim but lacks these precise technical details.
